common_name: Ronde de Valence Eggplant (French Heirloom Round Purple-Black Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant only once nights stay reliably warm; Ronde de Valence is an early, rustic French variety that sets fruit well even on the shorter side of the eggplant season.

directions: Ronde de Valence is a traditional French market eggplant named for the city of Valence on the Rhône, long grown in home gardens of southern France for its smooth, glossy, deep purple-black fruit that fades to pale greenish-white at the stem end. The medium-sized rounded fruits form on compact, rustic, heavily productive plants that tolerate variable conditions better than many finicky heirloom types. Grow it in full sun on fertile, well-drained soil with even moisture, and harvest while the skin is still glossy and taut for the sweetest, least bitter flesh. Its round shape and creamy, non-bitter interior make it a good all-purpose eggplant for stuffing, grilling, or classic ratatouille.

common_name: Purple Pickling Eggplant (Thornless Italian Heirloom Pear-Shaped Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; Purple Pickling is a midseason variety, so transplant promptly once soil and nights are reliably warm to give the longer fruit-set time it needs.

directions: Purple Pickling is a traditional Italian heirloom grown on distinctive purple-stemmed, thornless plants that make harvest easier than most eggplant varieties. It bears abundant pear-shaped, deep purple fruit up to 8 inches long, maturing a bit later than many standard types at around 90 days from transplant. Despite its name the fruit is equally good roasted, grilled, baked, or stewed fresh, with pickling and relish-making as its traditional specialty use. Keep plants picked regularly, since thornless stems make frequent harvest of young, glossy fruit simple and encourage continued production through the season.

common_name: Bonica Eggplant (French-Bred Hybrid Glossy Purple-Black Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant once nights stay above 60 F; Bonica is an early, heavy-cropping hybrid well suited to tunnels or protected culture in cooler climates as well as open-field growing.

directions: Bonica is a widely grown French-bred F1 hybrid valued across Europe for its tall, vigorous plants and exceptionally heavy, early cropping. It produces long, oval fruit around 6 inches long with deep purple, glossy skin and tender, mild-flavored flesh that holds its quality well. The vigorous habit benefits from staking or caging and steady feeding, since plants continue setting fruit heavily through a long season once established. Grow it in full sun with consistent moisture, and harvest fruit while still glossy for the best texture and flavor.
sources: Thompson & Morgan — Aubergine Bonica F1 Hybrid Seeds

common_name: Nigral Eggplant (Improved Early Black Italian Hybrid Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant once nights stay reliably above 60 F; Nigral is bred to set fruit reliably even under variable early-season conditions, giving some flexibility on transplant timing.

directions: Nigral is a modern F1 hybrid bred as an earlier-maturing, more reliable improvement on classic black Italian eggplant types, reaching harvest about a week sooner than comparable standard hybrids. The spineless plants carry a green calyx and set glossy, deep purple-black fruit up to 6 inches long even when spring weather is cool or inconsistent. Its dependable fruit set and compact habit make it a good choice for growers who want classic Italian eggplant character without the lower yields of older heirloom black types. Harvest while the skin remains glossy and firm, and pick regularly to keep plants flowering and setting new fruit.
